requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is satisfied.** The implementation, tests and documentation cover every obligation.

**Implementation** (`src/outline/rust.rs`, all marked `{impl}`):
- **Outline nodes.** `KINDS` maps every required item kind to an outline kind:
  - fn (`function_item` and `function_signature_item`), struct, enum, union, trait, impl, mod, const, static;
  - type (`type_item` and `associated_type`), macro (`macro_definition`), extern (`foreign_mod_item`).
  - It also maps item-position `macro_invocation`, `extern_crate_declaration` and `use_declaration`.
  - Methods are `function_item` nodes inside an impl or trait, so their selectors carry the ancestry, e.g. `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`.
- **Named by field.** Items named by the grammar `name` field produce `kind[name]` segments such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]`. Because the profile maps only syntactic nodes, ancestry is purely within the file. `mod foo;` is a leaf `mod[external]`, and nothing in `rust.rs` resolves modules across files.
- **Impls.** `impl_name` names an impl by the `type` field text and, when present, the `trait` field text. That gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` becomes `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`. Names are percent-encoded by the shared selector code, e.g. `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`.
- **Extern blocks.** `extern_name` uses the ABI string, or `Rust` when it is absent.
- **Anonymous items.** `use_declaration` and item-position macro invocations are `NameRule::Anonymous`, so they get `kind@hash` selectors. `item_macro` and `in_item_list` restrict macro nodes to item position, so expression macros in function bodies are not nodes.
- **Documentation.** `md/reference.md` has an "Outline profiles" table covering all Rust kinds and their naming. Its References section documents the selector spelling, the `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` form, anonymous `use@…`, and that modules are never resolved across files. The authoring `habeas` tool description also documents `impl[Thing/Trait]`.
- **Marking.** The rule-bearing items (`impl_name`, `extern_name`, `in_item_list`, `item_macro`, `KINDS`, `PROFILE`) all carry `{impl}`. The other helpers in `rust.rs` carry `{impl}` only for other definitions (`outlines`, `outline_comments`, `structural_hash`), and none of them adds selector-naming behaviour.

**Tests** (`src/outline/tests.rs`):
- **`rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`** checks every required kind and the selector round-trip:
  - mod, struct, enum, union, const, static, type alias, macro_rules and extern crate;
  - inherent and trait impls, trait methods and associated types;
  - an array-type self type with percent-encoding, extern with and without an ABI, and nested fns;
  - duplicate names disambiguated as `#1`/`#2`.
  - It also checks that `outline.resolve` accepts each selector, that the empty selector is the root, and that an ambiguous or missing selector is an error.
- **`selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates`** adds anonymous, distinct `use@` selectors.
- **`item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not`** checks:
  - anonymous macro selectors in item, impl-body and module positions;
  - a generic impl name, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`;
  - that expression macros inside a function body are not nodes.
- **Cross-file module resolution.** There is no `{test}` for "MUST NOT resolve modules across files" on this requirement. `mod[external]` appears as a leaf in the tests above. A separate test, `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file`, covers the `selector_inline_and_foreign` example. The behaviour is an absence, so this is adequate.

No unmarked implementation code or unspecified behaviour was found.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
